ideas.title: Blanket fort movie night
ideas.description: Build a fort out of every blanket and pillow in the house, string some lights inside, and watch a movie you both loved as kids. Popcorn is mandatory; the fort's architecture is up for debate.

ideas.title: Cook a cuisine you've never tried
ideas.description: Spin a globe (or pick a country at random), find one main dish and one dessert from there, shop for the ingredients together, and cook it side by side. Put on music from that country while you eat.

ideas.title: Homemade pizza night
ideas.description: Make the dough from scratch (or cheat with store-bought), set out every topping you can find, and each build a pizza for the other person. Rate them like a cooking show judge.

ideas.title: Blind taste test
ideas.description: Each of you buys five chocolates, chips, or sodas the other hasn't tried. Take turns blindfolded, guessing and ranking them. Keep score, and the winner picks the next date.

ideas.title: Board game tournament
ideas.description: Pick three games, play best of three in each, and keep a scoreboard on the fridge. Snacks between rounds, and a prize for the champion that you agree on before the first roll.

ideas.title: Jigsaw puzzle and a shared playlist
ideas.description: Open a 500-piece puzzle, make a playlist where you take turns adding songs, and see how far you get before the music runs out. No phones, just talking and finding edge pieces.

ideas.title: Paint each other's portraits
ideas.description: Set up two canvases (or paper), sit across from each other, and paint each other in 30 minutes. The worse they turn out, the better. Do a big reveal, then hang them on the fridge.

ideas.title: At-home spa night
ideas.description: Dim the lights, light a candle, put on face masks, and trade hand or shoulder massages. Add warm towels from the dryer and cucumber water, and leave your phones in another room.

ideas.title: Backyard stargazing nest
ideas.description: Drag blankets and pillows into the backyard (or onto a balcony), turn off every light you can, and give your eyes 20 minutes to adjust. Use a star app to find constellations, and stay out for a meteor shower if one's on.

ideas.title: Living room picnic
ideas.description: Spread a blanket on the floor, fill a basket with finger foods, fruit, and cheese, and have a picnic indoors. It works best when it's raining or snowing outside.

ideas.title: Dessert bake-off
ideas.description: Same recipe, two kitchens' worth of personality: you each make your own version of cookies, brownies, or cupcakes, with one secret ingredient. Taste-test blind and argue about the winner.

ideas.title: Learn a dance from a video
ideas.description: Pick a salsa, swing, or ballroom tutorial online, push the furniture aside, and learn the basic steps together. Expect stepped-on toes; finish with a slow song.

ideas.title: Living room karaoke
ideas.description: Pull up karaoke versions online, use a hairbrush for a mic, and take turns picking each other's songs. Bonus points for duets and dramatic key changes.

ideas.title: Letters to future you
ideas.description: Each write a letter to the two of you one year from now: what's happening, what you hope for, a memory from this month. Seal them with a date on the envelope and put them somewhere safe.

ideas.title: Plan your dream trip
ideas.description: Pick a place you'd both love to go, and plan the whole trip as if money and time didn't matter: flights, where you'd stay, three restaurants, one adventure. Then plan a realistic version you could take this year.

ideas.title: Co-op video game night
ideas.description: Find a game you can only beat together, like a two-player puzzle game, and play on the same couch. Snacks within reach, and no blaming the other person (out loud).

ideas.title: Fondue night
ideas.description: Melt cheese for dinner and chocolate for dessert, and cut up everything you can think of to dip: bread, apples, pretzels, strawberries, marshmallows. Slow, a little messy, and made for talking.

ideas.title: The 36 questions
ideas.description: Work through the famous 36 questions meant to bring people closer, taking turns to answer each one. They start light and get deeper. Even couples who've been together for years find new things out.

ideas.title: Recreate your first date at home
ideas.description: Remake your first date as closely as you can with what's at home: the same food, the same music, maybe even the same outfits. Compare what each of you remembers about that night.

ideas.title: Breakfast for dinner, with pancake art
ideas.description: Make pancakes for dinner and use a squeeze bottle of batter to draw on the griddle: initials, animals, each other's faces. Add bacon, fruit, and way too much syrup.
